title: Token Pasting
concept: Token pasting macros automate identifier generation to reduce repetitive code

steps.title: Including stdio.h header
steps.explanation:
**`#include <stdio.h>`** -- Includes the header for `printf`.

In this lesson we learn the **`##` operator (Token Pasting)**.

steps.title: Macro definition 1: Variable generator
steps.explanation: **`#define MAKE_VAR(type, name) type var_##name`** -- `##` joins the left token (`var_`) with the right token (the actual value of `name`) to create a single new token. `MAKE_VAR(int, apple)` becomes `int var_apple`.

steps.title: Macro definition 2: Getter function generator
steps.explanation: **`#define GETTER(name) int get_##name() { return var_##name; }`** -- Uses `##` **twice** to simultaneously generate the function name and the variable name in the body. `GETTER(apple)` becomes `int get_apple() { return var_apple; }`.

steps.title: Preprocessor execution: Variable generation
steps.explanation: **`MAKE_VAR(int, apple);`** and **`MAKE_VAR(int, banana);`** -- The preprocessor joins tokens with `##` to produce actual C code: `int var_apple;` and `int var_banana;`.

steps.title: Preprocessor execution: Function generation
steps.explanation: **`GETTER(apple)`** and **`GETTER(banana)`** -- `##` produces complete function definitions: `int get_apple() { return var_apple; }` and `int get_banana() { return var_banana; }`.

steps.title: Starting main function
steps.explanation: **`int main() {`** -- At this point, the overall structure the compiler sees is: global variables `var_apple`, `var_banana` (macro-generated) + functions `get_apple()`, `get_banana()` (macro-generated) + `main()` (hand-written).

steps.title: Assigning a value to the generated variable
steps.explanation: **`var_apple = 100;`** -- Although this name was automatically created by `##` joining `var_` and `apple`, you use it exactly the same as if you had written `int var_apple;` directly.

steps.title: Calling the generated function
steps.explanation: **`printf("Apple: %d\n", get_apple());`** -- Calls the `get_apple()` function generated by `GETTER(apple)`. This function returns the current value of `var_apple`, so `100` is printed.

steps.title: Program termination
steps.explanation:
**`return 0;`** -- The program terminates.

`##` (Token Pasting) is a preprocessor operator that joins two tokens to create a new identifier. It can only be used inside `#define`.

quiz.question: What is the role of the macro operator ##?
options: Joining two tokens into one (Token Pasting)
quiz.explanation: The ## operator physically concatenates the tokens on its left and right to create new variable names, function names, etc.

misconceptions.wrong: The # operator and ## operator are the same.
misconceptions.correct: # converts an argument into a string (" "), while ## joins arguments into a code token.

keyTakeaway: Using the ## operator, you can automatically generate dozens of similarly patterned variables or functions with just a few lines of macros.
